facts.value: Celsus never saw his library. It was put up by his son Gaius Julius Aquila after Celsus died in 110.
facts.quote: never saw the building, which was erected by his son Gaius Julius Aquila after his death in 110
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://www.livius.org/articles/place/ephesus/ephesus-photos/ephesus-library-of-celsus/' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'never saw the building, which was erected by his son Gaius Julius Aquila after his death in 110'

facts.value: Burial inside a library, close to the market, is called remarkable by Livius. It was an honour suited to the founder of a city.
facts.quote: is remarkable: this was an honor befitting the founder of a city
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://www.livius.org/articles/place/ephesus/ephesus-photos/ephesus-library-of-celsus/' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'is remarkable: this was an honor befitting the founder of a city'

facts.value: The four facade statues are named Sophia, Arete, Ennoia and Episteme. Livius reads them as the virtues of Celsus, and says the originals are in the Ephesos Museum in Vienna.
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://www.livius.org/articles/place/ephesus/ephesus-photos/ephesus-library-of-celsus/' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'Sophia (wisdom), Arete (character), Ennoia (judgment), and Episteme (expertise)'

facts.value: Before the library, Celsus was a tribune in the Fourth Legion Scythica, consul in 92 and governor of Asia in 106-107.
